rules.name: Spoofing/jwt-verification-without-algorithm-allow

shortDescription.text: An anonymous internet attacker forges a JWT for any account because neither JWT verification path constrains the accepted algorithm.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous internet attacker forges a JWT for any account because neither JWT verification path constrains the accepted algorithm. `updateAuthenticatedUsers` calls `jwt.verify(token, publicKey, cb)` at lib/insecurity.ts:189 with no `algorithms` option, and `isAuthorized()` at lib/insecurity.ts:52 builds `expressJwt({ secret: publicKey })` the same way. The verification key is the RS256 public key loaded from `encryptionkeys/jwt.pub` at lib/insecurity.ts:20, which ships in the repository, so the attacker signs an HS256 token using that public key text as the HMAC secret and both verifiers accept it.

shortDescription.text: An anonymous attacker reaches the archive and markup parsers because server.ts:309 registers `POST /file-upload` with only multer and the parsing chain `handleZipFileUpload, handleXmlUpload, handleYamlUpload`, and the authorization block that installs `security.updateAuthenticatedUsers()` and the route guards does not begin until server.ts:354.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker reaches the archive and markup parsers because server.ts:309 registers `POST /file-upload` with only multer and the parsing chain `handleZipFileUpload, handleXmlUpload, handleYamlUpload`, and the authorization block that installs `security.updateAuthenticatedUsers()` and the route guards does not begin until server.ts:354. The image endpoints at server.ts:310 and server.ts:311 are registered in the same unguarded window; only `/rest/memories` at server.ts:312 carries `security.appendUserId()`. Registration order therefore places three attacker-reachable parsers outside the authentication boundary entirely.

shortDescription.text: An attacker who brute-forces or injects their way into an account leaves no attributable trace, because routes/login.ts:24 issues a session token without writing any security log entry, and the failure branch at routes/login.ts:50 returns 401 with no record either.

fullDescription.text: An attacker who brute-forces or injects their way into an account leaves no attributable trace, because routes/login.ts:24 issues a session token without writing any security log entry, and the failure branch at routes/login.ts:50 returns 401 with no record either. A repository-wide search for audit-log identifiers across lib and routes returned zero hits, and neither routes/login.ts nor routes/resetPassword.ts imports the logger at all, so successful logins, failed logins, and password resets cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

rules.name: Tampering/sql-injection

shortDescription.text: An anonymous attacker authenticates as any account because routes/login.ts:34 builds the login query by interpolating `req.body.email` directly into `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '...' AND password = '...'` and passes it to `models.sequelize.query`.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker authenticates as any account because routes/login.ts:34 builds the login query by interpolating `req.body.email` directly into `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '...' AND password = '...'` and passes it to `models.sequelize.query`. No parameter binding or escaping is applied, so a quote plus comment sequence in the email field truncates the password predicate and the first returned row is handed to `afterLogin` at routes/login.ts:48, which issues a full session token.

shortDescription.text: LLM01 — Prompt Injection: an anonymous caller overrides the chatbot's behavioural rules because routes/chat.ts:191 reads the entire `req.body.messages` array with no schema, role, or length validation and passes it verbatim to `streamText` at routes/chat.ts:206 alongside the trusted system prompt.

fullDescription.text: LLM01 — Prompt Injection: an anonymous caller overrides the chatbot's behavioural rules because routes/chat.ts:191 reads the entire `req.body.messages` array with no schema, role, or length validation and passes it verbatim to `streamText` at routes/chat.ts:206 alongside the trusted system prompt. Nothing filters attacker-supplied entries with `role: 'system'` or `role: 'assistant'`, so injected turns are indistinguishable from the server's own instructions. The coupon policy at routes/chat.ts:98-103 is prompt text only, with no check outside the model, so an injected instruction reaches the `generateCoupon` tool.

shortDescription.text: An anonymous attacker runs unbounded credential stuffing against `POST /rest/user/login` because server.ts:596 registers the route with only `login()` and no throttling middleware.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker runs unbounded credential stuffing against `POST /rest/user/login` because server.ts:596 registers the route with only `login()` and no throttling middleware. shortDescription.text: LLM10 — Unbounded Consumption: an anonymous attacker drives arbitrary spend at the external LLM provider because server.ts:638 registers `POST /rest/chat` with neither authentication nor rate limiting.

fullDescription.text: LLM10 — Unbounded Consumption: an anonymous attacker drives arbitrary spend at the external LLM provider because server.ts:638 registers `POST /rest/chat` with neither authentication nor rate limiting. routes/chat.ts:206 forwards the caller-supplied message array with no size cap and no output-token limit, while `stopWhen: stepCountIs(10)` at routes/chat.ts:209 permits ten model round-trips per request and `maxRetries` at routes/chat.ts:208 multiplies each of them. fullDescription.text: An attacker defeats the only password-reset throttle because the `keyGenerator` at server.ts:346 buckets requests by `headers['X-Forwarded-For'] ?? ip`, a value the client fully controls. With `app.enable('trust proxy')` set at server.ts:342 and no trusted-proxy allowlist, rotating the header on each request places every attempt in a fresh bucket, so the 100-request window configured at server.ts:344-345 never triggers. The reset handler at routes/resetPassword.ts:41 then permits unlimited security-answer guessing, and a correct guess sets a new password at routes/resetPassword.ts:44.

fullDescription.text: LLM06 — Excessive Agency: routes/chat.ts:184 issues a real, redeemable coupon from a discount value the model chose, with no server-side bound and no authorization of the caller. The tool's input schema at routes/chat.ts:179 declares `z.number()` with the ten percent cap stated only in the description text and in the prompt policy at routes/chat.ts:98-103, so nothing outside the prompt constrains the value. Combined with the unauthenticated route at server.ts:638 and the unvalidated message array at routes/chat.ts:191, an anonymous caller injects an instruction that makes the model call the tool with an arbitrary discount.

message.text: Any GitHub user who can comment on a pull request triggers the privileged rebase job, because the condition at .github/workflows/rebase.yml:10 tests only that the thread is a pull request and that the comment body contains `/rebase`, and never checks github.event.comment.author_association or the commenter's repository permission. The issue_comment event runs the workflow from the default branch with repository secrets and the GITHUB_TOKEN passed to cirrus-actions/rebase on line 19, which fetches the pull request head and force-pushes a rewritten branch.

description.text: Enforce server-side authorization on every endpoint

message.text: An attacker edits the localStorage 'token' entry to a JWT whose payload claims data.role = 'admin', and AdminGuard admits the route because tokenDecode() uses jwtDecode, which reads the payload without verifying the signature; the administration and accounting views and their privileged API-calling code then load in the attacker's browser.

description.text: Enforce authorization on the server

message.text: An attacker reads any minter address from the public Sepolia NFT contract, then POSTs that address as walletAddress to /rest/web3/walletNFTVerify. The handler takes the wallet identity straight from the request body and looks it up in addressesMinted without ever asking the caller to sign a nonce with the corresponding private key, so the attacker is credited with a mint performed by a wallet it does not control.

description.text: Require a signed nonce challenge before accepting walletAddress in routes/nftMi…

trustBoundaries.rationale: The boundary assumes every request crossing it carries an authenticated identity, but this handler derives the acting wallet identity from the request body alone.

message.text: An attacker appends an allowlisted URL as a query parameter of its own host, for example /redirect?to=https://evil.example/?r=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. security.isRedirectAllowed accepts the value because it tests url.includes(allowedUrl) rather than an exact or origin match, and routes/redirect.ts:19 then issues a 302 to the attacker host from the application's own trusted origin.

description.text: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist

message.text: An attacker who controls the cli-assets.heroku.com distribution point serves a modified install.sh, which .github/workflows/ci.yml:358 pipes straight into sh with no checksum, signature, or pinned version. The script executes in the heroku job that goes on to deploy production with secrets.HEROKU_API_KEY on line 371, so the substituted code both runs on the runner and can read the deployment credential.

description.text: Pin third-party dependencies to immutable versions

message.text: An attacker who controls the configured product image or blueprint URL, or who intercepts the fetch, supplies arbitrary bytes that the seeding routine writes straight into the served asset directory, because downloadToFile is called with no checksum, signature, or content-type verification.

description.text: Verify token signatures before trusting claims

message.text: An attacker exploiting any of the confirmed HTML-injection sinks faces no script-source restriction, because the SPA shell declares no Content-Security-Policy: a grep of frontend/src for a CSP or any http-equiv meta directive returns zero hits, so injected inline handlers and external script loads both execute, and the page can also be framed for clickjacking.

description.text: Declare a script-src and frame-ancestors policy for the SPA shell

message.text: The bundle-analysis job sets its committer to a synthetic `GitHub Action <action@github.com>` identity at .github/workflows/frontend-bundle-analysis.yml:61 and then commits and pushes to master on line 66 without a commit signature. An attacker with any write path into the repository can commit under identical author and committer fields, and a reviewer reading the master history has no signature or account link that distinguishes the pipeline's commit from the forged one. The `continue-on-error: true` on line 67 additionally leaves the run green when the push is rejected.

description.text: Add security audit logging

message.text: A user opens developer tools, rewrites the localStorage 'email' entry to another person's address, and every subsequent API call carries X-User-Email with that forged value, because the interceptor copies browser-writable storage into an identity header on all outgoing requests; any server-side record or decision keyed on that header then names the wrong account.

description.text: Stop sending a client-asserted identity header from request.interceptor.ts

message.text: LLM07 — System Prompt Leakage: routes/chat.ts:105 places a rule marked `CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL ONLY` describing an undisclosed 15 percent courtesy discount into the system prompt that `buildSystemPrompt` returns and routes/chat.ts:205 sends to the external provider on every request. Because the message array is attacker-controlled (routes/chat.ts:191) and the endpoint is unauthenticated at server.ts:638, any caller can instruct the model to repeat its instructions and recover the confidential clause together with the full coupon policy.

description.text: Stop exposing internal information to clients

message.text: LLM02 — Sensitive Information Disclosure: routes/chat.ts:228 writes every tool-call event, including the tool name and the JSON-serialised model input, into the SSE response for every caller. The only role and cookie test in that branch is the `challengeUtils.solveIf` predicate at routes/chat.ts:225, which merely records progress and does not gate the write, so the `show_tool_calls` cookie and the admin role comparison have no effect on what is emitted. Anonymous callers therefore observe the internal tool inventory and the exact arguments the model chose.

description.text: Stop exposing internal information to clients

message.text: An anonymous caller retrieves the application's administrative configuration because server.ts:607 registers `GET /rest/admin/application-configuration` with only `utils.asyncHandler(retrieveAppConfiguration())` and no authorization middleware. No `app.use('/rest/admin', ...)` guard exists anywhere in the router, and the neighbouring version endpoint at server.ts:606 is equally open, so the whole `/rest/admin` prefix is reachable without a token.

description.text: Stop exposing internal information to clients

trustBoundaries.rationale: The boundary assumes every protected route sits behind expressJwt, but the admin configuration route is registered with no authentication middleware at all.

message.text: An attacker harvests stack traces, file paths, and library versions because server.ts:682 mounts `errorhandler()` as the terminal Express middleware with no environment guard, and server.ts:730 sets its title from the application name and Express version. Every route that forwards a failure through `next(error)` — for example the raw SQL failure path at routes/login.ts:53 — reaches this handler, so a malformed injection payload returns the underlying SQLite error and the server-side call stack to the caller.

description.text: Return generic error messages to clients

message.text: A user changes their password and the current and new plaintext passwords travel in the request URL, because routes/changePassword.ts reads them from query.current and query.new; anyone with access to reverse-proxy access logs, browser history, or a Referer header captured by a third-party asset on the page recovers those credentials verbatim.

description.text: Move password-change credentials from the query string to the request body

message.text: Dockerfile USER directive (non-root): Containers running as root expand container-escape blast radius.

description.text: Drop unnecessary privileges in build and runtime

message.text: Container image signing via cosign or attest-build-provenance: Unsigned container images cannot be verified for provenance — any registry intermediary could substitute them.

description.text: Sign and verify release artifacts

message.text: Dockerfile npm/pnpm/yarn install without --ignore-scripts: Without --ignore-scripts, any compromised dependency publisher can execute postinstall code at build time.

description.text: Disable untrusted package install scripts

message.text: GitHub Actions workflow-level permissions block: Without an explicit permissions block, the workflow inherits the repository default (commonly write-all) for GITHUB_TOKEN — any compromised step can push code, create releases, or approve PRs.

description.text: Apply least-privilege permissions

message.text: Third-party GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHA: Tag-based action references (@v3, @main) are mutable — a compromised publisher can retroactively inject malicious code into an already-used tag.

description.text: Pin third-party dependencies to immutable versions

message.text: Dockerfile base image must be digest-pinned: Tag-only base images (FROM node:24) can be silently substituted by a malicious publisher. Digest-pinning (@sha256:…) ensures the exact image bytes are used on every build.

description.text: Pin the container base image to an immutable digest

message.text: package-lock.json present and committed: Without a lockfile, `npm install` installs different transitive versions on each run — supply-chain attacks become undetectable.

description.text: Pin the container base image to an immutable digest

message.text: An attacker opens the shipped JavaScript bundle, reads the literal account name and password compiled into LoginComponent, and submits them to /rest/user/login to obtain a session without any guessing.

description.text: Move secrets to a managed secret store

message.text: An attacker reads or replays the duplicate session cookie the SPA writes itself, because cookieService.put('token', ...) is called from JavaScript with only an expiry, so the cookie is by construction not HttpOnly and carries neither Secure nor SameSite, leaving it readable by injected script and attachable to cross-site requests.

description.text: Set secure session-cookie attributes

message.text: An attacker repeatedly authenticates or replays distinct valid tokens; each one is inserted into the process-local tokenMap at lib/insecurity.ts:74, which has no size cap, no expiry sweep and no removal on logout, so resident memory grows monotonically until the Node process is killed by the allocator.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: Any internet user can open and then repeatedly update a pull request against the public repository, and the pull_request trigger at .github/workflows/ci.yml:14 starts frontend-test, server-test and api-test, each a three-operating-system by three-Node-version matrix whose test steps retry up to three times, alongside the e2e, smoke, docker-test and custom-config jobs. The workflow declares no concurrency group, so each new commit the attacker pushes queues another full set of runners instead of cancelling the previous run.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: An attacker opens many anonymous sockets and floods `verifySvgInjectionChallenge` with maximum-size payloads. Each event runs a backtracking regular expression carrying a leading `.*` and a lazy `[\w/-]*?` quantifier over the whole attacker-controlled string, synchronously on the single Node event loop that also serves the REST API on port 3000. Neither a payload size option nor any per-socket or per-connection event rate limit is configured, so the attacker converts cheap event emission into stalled request handling for every other user.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: An attacker submits very large comment bodies repeatedly and grows the single SQLite file until the host filesystem fills, because the comment column declares no length validator and SQLite does not enforce the declared string type, so nothing bounds the bytes written per row.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: An attacker sends a stream of unauthenticated POSTs to /rest/web3/walletExploitAddress, each carrying a distinct walletAddress string. routes/web3Wallet.ts:16 adds every value to the process-global walletsConnected set before any validation, and entries are removed only when a matching on-chain ContractExploited event arrives, so the set grows without any cap, eviction, or expiry until the Node process exhausts its heap.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: The release workflow declares no permissions block at workflow or job level, so the GITHUB_TOKEN handed to softprops/action-gh-release at .github/workflows/release.yml:20 and to Gamesight/slack-workflow-status on line 108 is issued with the repository's default scope rather than the contents: write that publishing a release needs. Any step in the packaging matrix that an attacker reaches, through the unlocked `npm install --production` on line 55 or a compromised action, inherits that broader write access to contents, packages, issues and pull requests.

description.text: Apply least-privilege filesystem access

message.text: An attacker who reaches any query path, including one opened by an injection flaw elsewhere in the process, operates with full authority over every table, because a single Sequelize connection created once at module load serves all access levels and SQLite enforces no per-principal or row-level permission.

description.text: Apply least-privilege filesystem access
